rationale: Archive Waihonu Solar Farm from the manager-level PortCo census and retire its Argo ownership period in 2025, while preserving the separately published Hawaiʻi Gas platform. Waihonu is the collective name for the Waihonu North and Waihonu South solar project assets, not a separate operating platform. Argo acquired the assets with Hawaiʻi Gas on July 21, 2022. Hawaiʻi Gas now states that Waihonu was acquired by a solar energy provider in 2025, and Form EIA-860 reporting changed from the two Waihonu project entities in 2024 to ERCAM LLC as the reporting utility and operator for both plants in the 2025 early release. The projects remain operational, but no reviewed source identifies ERCAM as an infrastructure-fund manager or supports adding a new manager ownership period. A redirect from Waihonu to Hawaiʻi Gas would be false because the project assets and utility platform are distinct identities. The exact 2025 closing date, transaction value and ERCAM parent are not publicly disclosed; those disclosure gaps do not block the list correction. No later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 16, 2026.

beforeImage.name: Waihonu Solar Farm
beforeImage.description: Waihonu Solar Farm is an operating solar generation asset on Oahu. The project supports Hawaii's clean energy supply and forms part of the broader energy platform associated with Hawaiʻi Gas. Its model is asset-heavy and based on ownership of an operating solar plant rather than development-stage activity. Hawaiʻi Gas describes Waihonu as one of Oahu's larger active solar farms with a combined output of 6.5 MW from 26,232 solar modules on about 12 acres in Mililani. The project was dedicated in 2016, and Argo acquired it indirectly as part of the 2022 purchase of Hawaiʻi Gas and related smaller energy businesses.

afterImage.name: Waihonu Solar Farm
afterImage.description: Waihonu Solar Farm is the collective name for Waihonu North Solar, a 5.0 MW photovoltaic plant, and Waihonu South Solar, a 1.5 MW photovoltaic plant, in Mililani on Oʻahu. The operating projects comprise 26,232 modules on approximately 12 acres and sell electricity to Hawaiian Electric under a power purchase agreement. Argo Infrastructure Partners acquired Waihonu as an underlying asset in its July 21, 2022 purchase of Hawaiʻi Gas and related businesses. Hawaiʻi Gas states that a solar energy provider acquired Waihonu in 2025, and the 2025 early-release Form EIA-860 data reports ERCAM LLC as the utility and operator for both plants. The projects remain operational, but no reviewed source establishes ERCAM as an infrastructure-fund manager. Waihonu is therefore realized and archived from the manager-level PortCo census without a redirect; Hawaiʻi Gas remains a distinct published platform. The exact 2025 closing date, transaction value and ERCAM parent are not publicly disclosed, and no later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 16, 2026.

milestones.event: The 6.5 MW Waihonu Solar and Sheep Farm was dedicated in Mililani, comprising the Waihonu North and Waihonu South photovoltaic projects.
Argo Infrastructure Partners completed its acquisition of Hawaiʻi Gas and related smaller energy businesses, including the Waihonu solar projects.

Hawaiʻi Gas reported that a solar energy provider acquired Waihonu; Form EIA-860 subsequently reported ERCAM LLC as the utility and operator for both plants. The exact closing date and transaction value were not publicly disclosed.
